Subject: Q2 usage drop + renewal window (HavenHealth / HB-3921)

Mina / Karthik —

Thanks again for taking a look at our Q2 run rate. We attached the raw token and endpoint logs from our team in case that helps. Quick summary from our side:

- Token spend dropped ~24% MoM in June after we reweighted the model mix to smaller variants; however latency-sensitive flows still push high-priority traffic to the larger model.
- We're seeing two predictable weekly spikes tied to batch ingest jobs (Tue 03:00 UTC and Fri 18:00 UTC).
- Renewals for our annual contract come up in mid-August; we'd like to lock something that gives us predictable headroom (burst credits or a small committed uplift) while avoiding a large upfront increase.

Goals for a short call this week:
- Quick readout on where commit vs run-rate sits and a recommendation for a 3–6 month bridge.
- Any immediate ops fixes on KV caching or batching you recommend so we don't overspend during bursts.
- A high-level ROI recap that shows unit-cost delta for the proposed term options.

Attached: HAVEN_Q2_usage_report.pdf (summary export).

Can you do 30 min on Wed Jul 22 09:00–11:00 PT or Thu Jul 23 14:00–16:00 PT? Prefer Mina as primary for commercial recs and Karthik for the ops readout.

—Andrew
Andrew Blake
Head of Growth Ops, HavenHealth
attachment: HAVEN_Q2_usage_report.pdf
From: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
To: Andrew Blake <andrew@havenhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q2 usage drop + renewal window (HavenHealth / HB-3921)

Andrew —

Thanks for the report and the clear asks. I pulled an initial cost model and attached RH_initial_cost_model.xlsx with two short scenarios:

1) Commit + burst credits (3-month bridge): adds 20% committed tokens, includes 15% burst pool for spikes. Estimated unit-cost reduction ~12% vs current overage.
2) Conservative roll-forward (no commit increase, auto-burst): keep current commit, add scheduled caching rules + ops optimizations estimated to reduce billable tokens by ~8% over 30 days.

My quick read: the commit uplift is the cleanest way to reduce unit cost and give predictability, but we can combine a small uplift with ops work if you want lower immediate spend. Karthik and I flagged the two weekly batch windows as the best place to apply a short-lived scheduled cache/aggregate flow to cut duplicated requests.

I can present the model and recommended language for a 3-month amendment in a quick call. Wed Jul 22 09:30 PT works for me (I blocked 09:30–10:00 PT). Proposal for agenda: 1) 10-minute usage & cost readout (me), 2) 10-minute ops mitigation plan (Karthik), 3) 10-minute term recommendation and next steps (Marissa for contracting).

Links: HubSpot deal HB-3921 (https://hubspot.company/deal/HB-3921). I've also added a shared folder with the model and the runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cDqHavenShared

Attached: RH_initial_cost_model.xlsx

Cheers,
Mina Haddad
Senior Director, Commercial (Renewals)
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q2 usage drop + renewal window (HavenHealth / HB-3921)

Andrew / Mina —

Quick ops note ahead of the call:

- The two spikes look like batch replays hitting the same prompt templates with minimal context changes. We can reduce billable tokens by ~18% for those windows by batching the ingest and enabling prefix KV caching on the affected endpoints.
- Latency for the smaller model at 95th pct remains <120ms in our hosted region; larger-model tail latency is the primary driver for cost because of longer token outputs on those flows. If you can control routing so that non-latency-critical jobs use the smaller model, that will materially reduce spend.
- I uploaded a short ops checklist to the shared Drive: redwood_ops_runbook_v2.xlsx — it has a recommended caching TTL and suggested batch sizes for your typical payloads.

I'll cover the implementation steps live on the call and propose a 72-hour pilot for batching that we can monitor in the console.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
--
